chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I asked Amr ibn Ubayd about the divorce of Ibn Umar, and he said: He divorced her while she was in a state of menstruation (taharah), one time.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Did you not say to him, 'When he divorced her once, whether she was menstruating or not, he has the right to take her back (raj'ah)?'
He said, 'I had said that to him.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He lied against him, may the curse of Allah be upon him. Rather, he divorced her three times.'
So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) returned her (to the state of being divorced once), and he said: 'Keep her or divorce her upon the Sunnah, if you intend to divorce.'

key_terms.رَجْعَة: Right of revocation/returning the wife without a new contract

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce during menstruation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the physical act of divorce and its legal validity by recounting the famous case of Ibn Umar, who divorced his wife during her menses. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the Prophet (PBUH) treated it as a single revocable divorce to maintain marital stability, the act itself constituted three divorces, a nuance that differentiates Shia fiqh from the Sunni view which often considers it a single 'Sunnah' divorce. This incident serves as the primary evidence for the concept of 'Talaq al-Ghar'' (irregular divorce) and underscores the importance of adhering to the Prophet's practical application of the Sunnah.
